units.title: The ferry across the blue mat
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The ferry across the blue mat
materials.text: Leo puts a blue mat on the floor and calls it a river. His toy cars wait on one side. He uses a wide lid as a ferry, moving it slowly across the mat. His sister makes a paper sign that says Ferry. One red car is too wide for the lid, so Leo leaves it beside the river and carries the smaller cars first. He does not push the red car into the pretend water. Later, he finds a wider tray for a second ferry. The red car can cross on that one. At the end, the cars and trays return to their boxes.

questions.prompt: Leo uses a blue mat as a pretend river.
questions.explanation: The mat is named as the river.

questions.prompt: The first ferry is a wide lid.
questions.explanation: The lid carries the first toy cars.

questions.prompt: His sister makes a paper bridge.
questions.explanation: She makes a Ferry sign, not a bridge.

questions.prompt: The red car fits on the first ferry.
questions.explanation: It is too wide for that lid.

questions.prompt: A wider tray carries the red car later.
questions.explanation: The second ferry is a tray that fits it.

units.title: The scarf on the chair
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The scarf on the chair
materials.text: Mia brings a long purple scarf to school for a play. After the rehearsal, she cannot find it in her bag. She asks the teacher before looking around the hall. Her friend remembers seeing it on a chair beside the piano. They go there together, but only a blue coat is on the chair. Then the teacher opens a storage box nearby. The scarf is inside with the other play clothes. Another adult had put it away to keep the room tidy. Mia thanks the teacher and checks the name label before taking it. The scarf goes back into her bag for the journey home.

questions.explanation: Its colour is stated in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Mia brings the scarf for a swimming lesson.
questions.explanation: It is for a play.

questions.prompt: The scarf is still on the chair when they look.
questions.explanation: The chair has a blue coat; the scarf is in a box.

questions.prompt: An adult had put the scarf with the play clothes.
questions.explanation: It was stored with the costumes.

questions.prompt: Mia checks the name before taking it.
questions.explanation: She checks the label after thanking the teacher.

materials.title: The round shape on the card
materials.text: Ben wants a round yellow shape on his card. He first draws one with a pencil, but it is smaller than he wants. Mum gives him a clean round lid and shows him how to draw around it. Ben holds the lid still while he moves the pencil along its edge. Now the circle is big enough. He colours it yellow and adds short lines around it to make a sun. His sister draws a small blue cloud beside it. They write a message inside the card for Grandpa. Before putting the lid away, Ben wipes it clean and checks that no pencil mark is left on the table.

questions.prompt: Ben wants a round yellow shape.

questions.prompt: His first circle is too big.
questions.explanation: It is smaller than he wants.

questions.prompt: Mum gives him a lid to draw around.
questions.explanation: The lid provides a circular edge.

questions.prompt: His sister draws a green tree.
questions.explanation: She draws a small blue cloud.
They write the message for Grandpa.

units.title: How a zip closes
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: How a zip closes
materials.text:
A zip fastener joins two flexible edges with rows of small teeth. The teeth do not simply sit beside one another: their shapes allow them to ____1____ when brought together by a slider. The result is a continuous fastening that can later be opened again.

The slider has internal channels that guide the two rows into the right ____2____. Moving it in one direction brings the rows together. Moving it the other way separates them. Its shape therefore controls a sequence, rather than holding every tooth itself.

For the mechanism to work, the teeth must be properly ____3____. A damaged or displaced section can interrupt the closing action. Pulling harder does not necessarily solve the problem and may make the damage worse.

The surrounding ____4____ also matters. Fabric caught near the slider can obstruct movement even when the teeth are sound. A user may need to stop and inspect the cause rather than treat every difficulty as a failure of the metal or plastic parts.

Different products make different ____5____ on a fastening. A small clothing zip and a heavy bag zip may share a principle while differing in size, material and construction. The chosen design needs to suit the intended ____6____.

A closed zip can ____7____ force along many joined teeth, but it still has limits. The fastening is not a reason to overfill a bag beyond what the product can handle. Care involves using the whole object ____8____, not only checking whether the slider reaches the end.

The mechanism is familiar partly because its useful action is ____9____: a short hand movement changes a long edge from open to closed. Understanding the parts makes that ordinary movement easier to explain. It also helps distinguish a temporary obstruction from damage that needs proper ____10____.

questions.explanation: Interlock means engage matching teeth; borrow and whisper cannot describe that action.
Alignment is the relative arrangement guided by the channels, not a material or repair.
Positioned describes teeth placed correctly; other entries do not form the required participial complement.
Material includes nearby fabric; the following sentence identifies the possible obstruction.
Demands are requirements imposed by the product; no other plural bank noun fits this requirement sense.
Intended use is the purpose to which size and construction should be suited.
Distribute means spread load along many teeth, not borrow or interlock force.
Sensibly describes appropriate use; silently concerns noise, not respecting capacity.
Visible describes the observable open-to-closed change; tropical concerns climate.
Repair addresses actual damage; alignment is a relation and recipe a set of food instructions.

units.title: When a catalogue search returns nothing
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: When a catalogue search returns nothing
materials.text:
An empty catalogue search can seem to offer a definite answer: the collection contains nothing relevant. That conclusion depends, however, on the relation between the search and the catalogue's ____1____. A database of descriptions is not necessarily a complete transcription of every document.

The words used in a query may differ from those used by the cataloguer. A modern place name may have an older ____2____, and a person may appear under initials. A search can therefore fail to ____3____ an item that is present but described differently.

The level of description matters too. A box-level entry may name a broad topic while omitting the names contained in individual letters. The absence of a name from the catalogue is not automatically ____4____ of its absence from the box.

A useful search strategy makes its ____5____ explicit. It records which catalogue, terms and filters were used. Without that information, another researcher cannot distinguish a careful unsuccessful search from a brief attempt with a narrow query.

This does not require treating every negative result as worthless. It requires a ____6____ account of what the result can support. Searching a well-defined, fully transcribed list may justify a stronger conclusion than searching a selective description of mixed papers.

Researchers can ____7____ their approach by trying variant names, broader categories or advice from collection staff. Each step should answer a particular limitation rather than expand the search indefinitely without purpose.

The final report can state that no matching entry was found under the specified conditions. That wording preserves the result without ____8____ it into a claim about every possible source. It also keeps the work ____9____ to later checking. A negative search becomes more informative when its boundaries are part of the ____10____ rather than hidden behind the word nothing.

questions.explanation: Coverage concerns how much of the collection the catalogue describes.
A variant is another form of a name; coverage and method do not name that alternative.
Retrieve is locate or bring back an entry in search.
Evidence of absence is the inference under discussion; method/report do not name evidential support.
Method records the search procedure and settings.
Qualified means appropriately limited, contrasting with a universal claim.
Refine means improve the targeted procedure; erase removes rather than improves it.
Inflating a result means enlarging its claim beyond its basis.
Open to checking is the required predicate-adjective expression; edible is irrelevant.
Report is the account in which search boundaries should appear.

units.title: Why a sponge holds water
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: Why a sponge holds water
materials.text:
A dry sponge contains many small spaces connected through its structure. When it meets water, liquid can enter those spaces. The amount held depends partly on the sponge's ____1____ and on how the material interacts with water.

The visible outline alone does not describe its useful ____2____. Two objects of similar size may differ in the number and arrangement of internal spaces. The material surrounding them also affects the result.

When a wet sponge is squeezed, its shape changes and some spaces become smaller. Water is ____3____ out as the available volume decreases. Releasing the pressure allows many sponges to regain much of their previous shape.

That recovery is not always ____4____. A worn or damaged sponge may behave differently from a new one. The force used and the material's condition affect how well it returns.

A sponge can be useful for spreading or removing liquid, but its ____5____ must be considered. Picking up water does not mean it destroys dirt or makes an unclean surface safe by itself. Cleaning involves more than the physical movement of liquid.

After use, retained water may remain in the ____6____. The way a sponge is cleaned, dried and replaced should follow suitable guidance for its task. The same object should not be moved carelessly between uses with different hygiene requirements.

A user may judge the sponge by how ____7____ it feels, but a full explanation involves internal structure and material behaviour. The familiar action of squeezing links a hand movement to a change inside an object we cannot see through.

Simple comparisons can help ____8____ that link. Observing water entering and leaving makes the process more concrete, even without measuring every pore. Such a demonstration should be described ____9____, with conclusions limited to what was actually compared. A useful everyday explanation connects an observable result with a plausible ____10____ while keeping the practical limits in view.

questions.explanation: Structure concerns the internal arrangement affecting water retention.
Capacity is how much can be held, which outline alone does not determine.
Forced out describes pressure expelling water.
Complete recovery contrasts with partial recovery in worn material.
Purpose is intended cleaning or liquid-handling task.
Pores are the small internal spaces that retain water.
Soft is the tactile adjective describing feel; complete does not name that sensory quality.
Illustrate makes a relationship concrete through demonstration.
Carefully limits the account to actual comparison; privately concerns audience only.
Mechanism explains how the observable result occurs.

units.title: The note beside a translated word
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: The note beside a translated word
materials.text:
A translator's footnote can make a difficult choice visible, but the presence of a note does not automatically make the choice ____1____. Readers still need to know what problem the note addresses and how it relates to the surrounding passage.

Some words have a range of associations that no single substitute can ____2____. A note may identify a cultural reference, explain a pun or describe an alternative reading. These are different functions, and combining them without distinction can obscure the translator's ____3____.

A useful note has an appropriate ____4____. Too little information may leave the difficulty untouched, while an extensive essay can interrupt a passage whose force depends on movement. The decision involves the work's purpose and likely readers, not a universal ideal number of words.

Notes also distribute ____5____. They draw attention to selected problems while leaving other choices unmarked. Readers should not assume that every unnoted expression passed between languages without interpretation.

In an introduction or statement of method, the translator can make the selection principles ____6____ rather than leaving them implicit. Such an account need not list every ordinary decision. It can explain the principles used to decide when a note was warranted.

A note may preserve an unresolved ____7____ rather than announce one certain answer. That is especially useful when the source itself permits more than one reading. Precision sometimes consists in identifying the uncertainty rather than removing it.

The reader can then ____8____ the proposed wording with a clearer sense of its limits. The note supports judgement; it should not demand automatic agreement. Good annotation remains ____9____ to correction as knowledge and interpretations develop. Its value is in making the translation's reasoning more ____10____, not in pretending that explanation ends the conversation.

questions.explanation: Correct means justified as a translation choice; a note alone cannot guarantee it.
Capture means convey the range of associations.
Intention is what the translator is trying to do with the note.
Scale concerns the amount and extent of explanatory material.
Attention is directed toward selected marked difficulties.
Explicit means stated openly, matching the proposed method account.
Ambiguity is the unresolved availability of more than one reading.
Assess means evaluate the wording; erase removes it.
Open to correction is the standard expression for revisability.
Accessible means available to understanding; edible is irrelevant and explicit is already used in its stronger stated-principle slot.

units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Write ONE word in each gap. Gap 0 is an example. Use capital letters; marking ignores case.

materials.title: A route through a museum
materials.text:
A museum route (0) IS a choice about sequence as well as space. Visitors may feel that they are simply walking through a building, ____1____ each doorway places one encounter before another. That order can shape the account they take away.

There is no point ____2____ pretending a route can include everything equally. Some objects receive a central position, while others remain at the edge. The useful question is not whether selection occurs, ____3____ how it is made and explained.

A route may move from early to late events, or from one theme to another. Neither arrangement speaks ____4____ itself. Labels and transitions help visitors understand what kind of connection they are being invited to make.

The account can be clear without claiming that every object has only one meaning. As ____5____ as practical access is considered, alternative paths may offer another way into the material. Visitors need not follow precisely the same sequence to find a thoughtful encounter.

The route should also leave room for someone ____6____ wants to pause, return or skip a section. Designing for an imagined average pace can overlook how differently people use a museum. To some ____7____, a successful route supports choices rather than merely directing feet. It helps visitors make sense of what they meet, while keeping them aware ____8____ the larger collection beyond the chosen path.

questions.explanation: But/yet contrast apparent simple walking with editorial order; while can mark the same contrast.
No point in pretending uses in.
Not whether ... but how contrasts the questions.
Speak for itself is the expression.
As long as introduces the practical-access condition.
Someone who/that forms a human subject relative.
To some extent/degree limits the claim.
Aware of takes of.

materials.title: A recipe with several owners
materials.text:
A family recipe (0) MAY be described as unchanged for generations, even when every cook remembers a different detail. One uses more water; another adds the spice later. The name stays familiar, ____1____ the practice continues to develop.

It is worth asking what people mean ____2____ unchanged. They may mean that the dish keeps a recognisable place in family life, not that every quantity is identical. A shared name can connect variations without making them the same in every respect.

No matter ____3____ carefully a recipe is written, it cannot specify every condition in a kitchen. Ingredients, equipment and the cook's judgement still matter. There is little point ____4____ treating the page as though it were the whole activity.

A useful record can preserve more ____5____ one version. It might name who used each method and when, rather than forcing the accounts into a single authoritative list. Disagreement then becomes part of the history rather than an error to erase.

The writer need not speak on ____6____ of every relative. It is enough to explain whose account has been recorded and where other versions differ. As ____7____ as those boundaries remain clear, a modest record can be both personal and useful. Its value lies partly in keeping a conversation available to people ____8____ have not yet learned the dish themselves.

questions.explanation: The conjunction contrasts continuity of name with change in practice.
Mean by a word asks its intended meaning.
No matter how carefully forms the adverbial construction.
Little point in treating uses in plus -ing.
More than one version uses comparative than.
On behalf of is the expression.
As long as sets a condition.
People who/that uses a human subject relative.
